answer: Each agent must register a unique physical utility meter at a fixed service address. A bonded inspector photographs the meter's saffron tamper seal and serial, and the ledger enforces one key per meter, slashing the deposit if a second key tries to echo the same serial. Extra identities cannot simply wander between addresses because each sybil needs a separate metered hookup and pays recurring site, electricity, and inspection costs; aggregate profit is n(R-C), so cloning pays only while per-identity reward exceeds that recurring cost. Inspector collusion or forged seals remain the weakness.
